utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, not always.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: When did you start living there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I started living there in 1980.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: What is your occupation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Policeman.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Which police force do you work in?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Police station Prijedor 1, Prijedor Jedan.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: What is your present job within the police?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Policeman for materiel, technical means and records.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: How long have you done that job for?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Since 1992.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: When in 1992 did you start that job?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sometime around 1st May 1992.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: What sort of records are you in charge of in the course of your work?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay, how much time do you estimate for, is it, Mr. Savic and for, is it, Mr. Budimir? They are new witnesses on the list.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. Your Honour, Savic, I estimate, will take slightly over half an hour perhaps. Budimir is not yet available and an affidavit has been filed in relation to him today as well as Savic. We have had to revise our order because of availability of witnesses. I do not know if it would help the Court if I just indicated what the order was now proposed to be?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: We can, since we are waiting for the video to come back on. Will Mr. Savic be the next witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. Savic would be next, then Reljic, then Smoljic, then Samardija -- no, sorry, then Gajic -- there has been a change in relation to that as well -- then Gajic, then Samardija and then Budimir at the end.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Samardija will be before Budimir?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. Because, apparently, this room is very hot here.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Andic?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Andic will not be called.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: So he will not be called. You indicated time for Mr. Savic a little over half an hour or so. I put down half an hour to an hour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your Honour, apparently, the room is very hot in Banja Luka where this is taking place and it can be uncomfortable for certain people to remain in there.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: So is that the reason why you have changed the order?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. Reljic's age, your Honour may recollect, an affidavit filed on his behalf.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: But you have him listed coming after Savic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. We are trying to find a moment so he does not have to wait all day.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: You have him listed after Savic and that is 1.5 hours?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Mr. Vujanovic, can you hear me now?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can hear you. I can hear you. I can hear you well.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: I will repeat the question that I asked before we were cut off. What types of records are you in charge of in the course of your work?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Exclusively records related to police and police duties and tasks.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Could the Exhibit which has been marked for identification as D74 be shown to the witness, that is No. A1? Mr. Vujanovic, I would ask you to look at a document and tell us whether you recognise it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I recognise it.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Can you tell us what it is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is the work list that is kept in the police.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: What is the date on that record?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This document pertains to the month of August 1992.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Whose handwriting appears on that document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The handwriting is personally mine.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this stage I would tender that document as an Exhibit and ask that copies be given to your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger, objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I think technically the foundation has not yet been laid, but I imagine that would ultimately go to the weight so I will not have any objection.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: OK. Defence 74 will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I could pass up to you both that document and the translation of that document? Perhaps we could mark them as 74A for the original and 74B for the English translation?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: 74A is in Bosnian, Serbo-Croatian.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Your Honour, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: And B is in English. The Prosecution has a copy, I presume? OK. 74A and B will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Mr. Vujanovic, can you tell us when you would have written the information contained in that document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The data that are entered into this document before the war, during the war and after the war. I mean, the system of keeping these records is the same. Data are entered a day behind. For example, today you give data for the previous day, for yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: So, this document would have been written during August 1992 and for each date that we have on the document it would have been filled in the day after that date, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is right, yes, a day after that.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Where did you get the information from that you put into this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The data entered into this document are based on the schedule that is worked out by the Commander of the station.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Who was the Commander of the station at this time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Commander of the station at that time was Milutin ----

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The English interpreter cannot hear the last name.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: If you could repeat the name of the Commander, Mr. Vujanovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Milutin Cadjo.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Where would you find the copies of that schedule, the information from which you would then put into this book?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: After entering the data from the daily schedule into the work list that I have before me, the schedules are kept for two years at most while the work list remains as a permanent document. So we do not have a copy of the document from which I took the data that I entered into this document.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Where would you see the schedule that you copied the list from when you copied it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The daily schedule is kept by the shift Commander, that is to say, the leader of the shift who sends people to duty on that particular day. The next day, the leader of the shift is supposed to give the schedule to the Commander and then he has a look at it and then gives it to me for further processing.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Would this schedule that you copied the data from be signed by anyone?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it was signed by the Commander of the station.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: When would that daily schedule have been drawn up?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A daily schedule is being drawn up a day in advance.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: A day in advance of the hours worked?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, today for tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: If a policeman failed to turn up for work or was sick, would that be noted on the daily schedule?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The leader of the shift would be duty bound to register this if a policeman would not report to duty.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Would that be registered on the schedule from which you copied these duty books?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It should be registered there.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: If it was registered there that someone had failed to turn up, would you write down the hours that they had originally been scheduled to do next to their name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I cannot enter those hours for a worker who was absent, who did not come to work, and what measures were to be taken further, that is up to the Commander. The Commander has to see why this person did not show up for work.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Did you have contact with the policemen whose duty schedules you wrote up in this book?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not have any need to be in contact with them.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Did you know Dusko Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I never knew him.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Mr. Vujanovic, what I would like you to do for us is to take us through the information on this schedule. You will see that several of the names have been redacted from that list, but that Dusko Tadic's name remains in full at No. 317. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I see it. I see it.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Could you tell us then what words appear after Dusko's name and under the dates from 1st to 6th August?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Could you please repeat your question? I did not quite understand it.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: If you look to the columns which appear after the name of Dusko Tadic, can you see that there are some words written across the first six columns?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Could you tell us what those ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I see it. I see it now.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Could you tell us what those words are? Your Honour, I think the witness has the English version in front of him and this could be what is causing the confusion. If the witness could be given the Serbo-Croat version of this document.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Marro, it should be Defence 74A that the witness should have.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARRO
utterances.text: He has the correct one.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Thank you. Is that in English or Serbo-Croatian?

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: It is document A1 if that is of any assistance.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARRO
utterances.text: It is in Serbo-Croatian.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Vujanovic, could you now tell us what words appear across the first six columns after Dusko Tadic's name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: After the name of Dusko Tadic, Miroslav, Milisav, Boro, Simo, Ljubisa, Mladen.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Mr. Vujanovic I am looking to the right of the document, the column which follows Dusko Tadic's name, all the way across the page. Could we ask that ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Worked -- I understand what you are asking now. Worked in the police station for control of traffic before coming to police station Prijedor 1, Prijedor Jedan.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Does that mean that Mr. Tadic had been transferred from the police station for the control of traffic to another post?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Precisely that. From the police station for traffic security he was transferred to Prijedor 1, Prijedor Jedan.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Can you tell us from that list on what day he first started working at police station Prijedor 1?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The first working day was August 7th 1992.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: I would like you to tell us, if you can, what the figures that are in that box for Dusko Tadic on August 7th 1992 mean. So if we could start with the figures at the top of that box which, I believe, is 06?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is not 06. It is 0B, security service, sluzba obezbedjenja. "OB" is the abbreviation used.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Vujanovic. Does that indicate where Dusko Tadic would have been working on that day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it indicates the place where he worked and the kind of service he was engaged in.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Can you tell us from that document which place he worked and what kind of service he was engaged in?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can only tell you now that he was involved in security, obezbedjenja. What facility, what building, that I cannot tell you. He could have been involved in the security of the police building itself, of Radio Prijedor or any other important building. I cannot tell what security he was involved in on that particular day.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell us what hours he worked on that day from that document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Please repeat your question because I did not fully understand it.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Does that document indicate what hours Dusko Tadic worked on 7th August?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It does. It does indicate his working hours.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Can you tell us ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From 14 to 2200 hours.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: The 8 which is underneath the 14 to 22, what does that mean?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is the total number of hours spent working that day.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Mr. Vujanovic, I would like you to help us in the same way with 8th August. Can you tell us what Dusko Tadic's duties were then from that list?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The same service as I said on the previous day, security, but from 16 to 18 which means that he spent eight hours working that day.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: The numbers there were not clear to me; from which hour to which hour was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From 6 to 14 hours.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Thank you. With regard to 9th August, can you tell us where and when he worked on that date?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Also security. I cannot tell. I do not know where he was working from 6 to 1400 hours.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: In the next box under 10th August, the figures P(iv) appear. Can you tell us what that means?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: P(iv) -- there is no 1 -- it is P(iv).

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Does that indicate where he would have been working on that day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It does. It does indicate the place where he was working.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Where was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: P is Pozorna sluzba. That is part of the city centre. It is the area of the bus station and railway station of Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: What does the (iv) mean?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Because in the city there are several such quarters, such parts, of the city. This is the designation for one of these parts of the city.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: So would I be correct in saying that P(iv) means that he was working at the bus and railway station of Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes, on 10th he was at the railway station from 2100 to 6 a.m.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: That would be 6 a.m. on 11th?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: If you could read in the line underneath that which is marked from 11th to 12th, what hours would Dusko be working that day and in what place?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On the same day at the same working place, he worked at the same -- in the same period from 21 hours to 6 a.m. that is to say, from 11th to 12th August.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: On 12th August?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On 12th August he worked until 6 a.m. On the same day he worked in the same area in the time period from 14 to 2100 hours.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: On 13th?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On 13th, on the same working place in the period from 14 to 2100 hours.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: The 14th?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: For the 14th, in the same working place from 06 to 1400 hours.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: On the 15th?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The 15th, the same working place, in the period from 6 to 1400 hours.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: The 16th?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The 16th, in the same working place from 2100 to 6.00 a.m.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Would that be to 6 a.m. on 17th?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Until 17th, 6 a.m.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: On 17th did he work again?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On 17th he also worked in the same working place from 2100 to 6 a.m. on 18th, that is, between 17th and 18th.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: On 18th did he work again?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On 18th again he worked from 14 to 2100 hours in the same place.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: The 19th?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Would you please repeat -- would you please repeat the date? I did not understand the date.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: 19th August?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On 19th in the same working place from 14 to 21.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: The 20th?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The 10th?

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: The 20th?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The 10th August?

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: No, 20th August.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 20th August, the 20th August, in the same working place from 06 to 1400 hours.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: 21st?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On 21st, the same working place in the period from 6 to 1400 hours.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: 22nd?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On 22nd the same working place from 2100 to 6.00 a.m.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Would that be 6 a.m. on 23rd?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Did he work again on 23rd?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On 23rd he worked again from 21 hours to 6 a.m. on 24th.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Did he work again on 24th?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On 24th he worked in the same working place from 14 to 2100 hours.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: 25th?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On 25th, at the same working place from 14 to 2100 hours.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: The 26th?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On 26th, in the same working place from 6 to 1400 hours.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: The 27th?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On 27th, at the same working place from 06 to 1400 hours.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: On 28th?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On 28th, at the same working place from 2100 to 6 a.m.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Is that 6 a.m. on 29th?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On 29th until 6 a.m.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Did he work again on 29th?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he worked again from 2100 to 6.00 a.m. the following day.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: The following day is 30th. Did he work again on 30th?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On 30th he worked again from 1400 to 2100 hours.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: On 31st?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On 31st, also from 1400 to 2100 hours.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Your Honour, I note the time and that is a convenient moment.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: We will stand in recess until 2.30.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Marro, we are ready for the witness. Miss de Bertodano, you may continue. I am not sure -- you can see whether he can hear us.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Mr. Vujanovic, at this point I would like you to look at another document and if we could have document B1 placed in front of the witness, please? Mr. Vujanovic, do you recognise that document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I recognise it.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: What is it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is an extract from the duty list for the month of September 1992.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Whose handwriting is on that exhibit?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is mine.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would ask that that Exhibit be marked and tendered as Exhibit 78. Again there is an English translation, so 78A for the original and 78B for the translation? We have three copies for your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Was this exhibit kept in the same way -- I gather it was. Is that so, Miss de Bertodano?

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: I am going to ask him that, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Mr. Vujanovic, when did you write the information that is in that document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I wrote in the information also one day later, that is, one day after the duty had been performed.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Where did you get the information from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I obtained the information from the daily timetable prepared by the station Commander.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: I would like you to help us with some of the information in that document. If you could look down to the second name up from the end, No. 203, and do you see "Tadic Dusko" written there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is so written.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: For the date of 1st September, can you tell us what that document says that Dusko Tadic was doing on that day?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Are you going to offer 78A and B?

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Your Honour, I thought I had.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Is there any objection to Defence Exhibit 78A and 78B?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: 78A and B will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: I think you can assume that the Judges follow it and you need not go through each day.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Very well, your Honour. Mr. Vujanovic, can you tell us for 1st September where Dusko Tadic was working, what he was doing and what hours from the information on that document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: According to this document, Dusko Tadic was working in the 4th district, that is, the region of the bus and railway station, from 06 to 1400 hours.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: For the subsequent days of 2nd and 3rd September and also the 6th to 8th September, was he also working in the region of the bus and railway station in the 4th district?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, throughout this period until September 8th he was working in the 4th district; only on 5th September he did not work one shift.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Is that what is written in the box under 5th September?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, the words "he did not work" have been written in.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: If we turn to 9th September and going along the column to 15th, can you tell us what is written in those boxes? Once again, your Honour, it seems that the English translation is in front of the witness rather than Serbo-Croat.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Vujanovic, do you have the English version of this Exhibit? Mr. Marro, would you see whether he has 78A or 78B?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARRO
utterances.text: Your Honour ----

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: I am sorry, your Honour, it appeared --

utterances.speaker: MR. MARRO
utterances.text: --- the witness has the Serbo-Croatian text and I put on the screen the English which is 78B, which is exactly the same, but we have one in Serbo-Croatian and the other one in English so you will always see the screen in English.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: I am sorry, your Honour, that is my fault. I saw it on the screen in English.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Marro. MISS DE BERTODANO (To the witness): Can you tell us what is written in the boxes from 9th to 15th September for Dusko Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The sound was lost for a moment.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: I am sorry, Mr. Vujanovic, we had a problem with the sound and I did not hear the first part of your answer. If I could ask you again to tell us what is written across that column?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: For 9th September, according to this duty schedule, he was to have worked in the shift from 21 hours and I think he did not come that day, but on the following day, on 10th, he was transferred to another station, that is, the Kozarac police station.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Can you tell us what words are written in the column of 9th September?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: "Did not come to work".

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Where would you have got that information from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This information is copied from the schedule prepared by the leader of the shift.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: From where would you have got the information that he was transferred to the Kozarac police station?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From the station Commander.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: The two documents that we have been looking at, can you tell us whether they are kept in a book?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they are kept in a book.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: What does this book record, apart from the information that we have been looking at?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Nothing else, except this information for each month separately throughout the year.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Does it record that information for all the policemen who were working for the station?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: For each individual policeman, this information is recorded.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Is the book headed in some way? Is there a title on the book?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is called a working list, radna lista.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Thank you. You told us that the daily schedule was kept by the shift Commanders, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The shift leader simply advises the policeman what duty he has to perform on that day on the basis of a schedule prepared by the station Commander.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: So the typed schedule from which you wrote this book was prepared by the station Commander?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: The shift leader would then convey that information to the people who were working?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The shift leader encircles the number under which the name of the person is listed if he has come to work, and if he has not come to work he writes the words "he has not come to work".

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Do you know who Dusko Tadic's shift Commander was at that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: After so much time I am afraid I cannot remember.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Nothing further, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Cross-examination, Mr. Tieger?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour. Mr. Vujanovic, I would like to begin by asking you a few background questions. First of all, what is your date of birth?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was born on 13th March 1955.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What is your father's name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Milos, Milos.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Do you have any brothers or sisters?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have a sister only.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What is her name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mirka Vujanovic -- Mirka Vujanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Where did you live before moving to Prijedor in 1980?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I lived for a time in the region of Bosanska Dubica and for a time in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Do you have any nicknames? Do you go by any names other than Mirko?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I do not.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Where were you living immediately before coming to Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I lived in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What was your occupation there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was a policeman there too.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What kind of duties did you perform in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I provided security for buildings and persons.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you have a particular title or rank?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The question is not clear to me. Could you repeat it, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Sure. In the role of providing security for buildings and persons, was that function identified by a particular title within the police department?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, it was a special police station for the security of more important buildings and persons.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What was that police station called?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The police station for security of persons and buildings.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: When you came to opstina Prijedor, did you immediately begin work for the Prijedor police?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I immediately started working in the public security station, but in the department, the police department of Ljubija.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What were your duties for the Ljubija police department?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were normal duties of policing.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Who was your Commander when you began work for Ljubija?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When I started working in Ljubija, my Commander was Krajisnik Mehmed -- Krajisnik Mehmed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Who was your last Commander at the Ljubija police station?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The last Commander was Vijekic Branko.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I believe you told us that on or around May 1st 1992 you became a member of the Prijedor police station, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: How many of your fellow officers from Ljubija became members of the Prijedor police station at that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Two.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What was their ethnic group or nationality?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What is your ethnic group, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Serb.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: After you began work for the Prijedor police station, were you immediately placed in charge of records and materiel, technical means?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, immediately.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Where were you working? Where was your physical location or your office?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the building of the secretariat of the public security station.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: That is sometimes known as the SUP?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, SUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Has that continued to be your office to this day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mostly, yes, although the actual offices have changed. I have changed to the one next door, but it is the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: In the spring and summer of 1992 what were your daily responsibilities or daily activities as the person in charge of the records and technical means?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My duties mostly had to do with supply of equipment, keeping these various records in the police and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you have any deputies or assistants?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was a colleague who would work with me from time to time and assist me.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What duties did he assist you with? What responsibilities did he sometimes help you with?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In supplies, in getting supplies. We would go together to get clothing for the workers and that sort of thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What is his name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Stakic Radenko.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Vujanovic, I am looking now at the Exhibit which has been marked D74 and which you have indicated is the August 1992 work list. Do you have that nearby?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I take it you are looking at that now, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Would you please repeat the question? I did not understand it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: It appears from the screen that you now have that document in front of you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do have it, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Looking at the row in which the name Dusko Tadic appears and going to the far right portion of that row, there is a column which is identified above which is column 7 as "primjedbe", do you see that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What does that refer to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This refers to the total number of hours worked. "P" means guard duty, 21 x 8 hours. I cannot see it too well. It is 184, 186 hours worked. Then again security, 3 x 8 hours, it should be 24.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Let me ask you to turn your attention to the column immediately to the right of that, the "remarks" column. I see that in the first person listed the remark or the information indicated in the "remarks" column is "unemployed", is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is information that we entered to facilitate our work. It is true that it says "unemployed" there.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What does that refer to? What does it mean with reference to that particular policeman?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is information that we provided for certain needs. We asked whether people were employed or unemployed, and so probably we entered only information for only those who were unemployed, just to facilitate our work. As a rule, one does not enter anything else there except the number of hours worked.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: You indicated during your earlier testimony that you filled in the information which is shown in this document the day after the work was supposed to be performed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: You took that information from the daily schedule prepared by the station Commander?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: So, in fact, I take it there was no particular need to record that information on the day after the work was supposed to be performed; it could have been written down two days later or three days later because the information which you had in front of you would have been the same?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I always kept this on a regular basis. I sought to perform my duty on a daily regular basis.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: There was no occasion on which you were sick or absent or occupied with other duties which caused you to fill in this form a day or two later?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, for this, these months of August and September I kept the records regularly. Perhaps in my absence my colleague that I mentioned kept the records before or after this period, but for this period I kept them on a daily basis.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Tieger, we are going to take an early recess because of a matter that has to be attended to. So we will stand in recess for 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Marro, you are bringing in the witness? Thank you. Mr. Tieger, you may continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Vujanovic, I would like to ask the Registrar to place Exhibit 78 in front of you and that is the September work list. Looking at the second column, No. 2, that refers to the position occupied by the particular police officer? Let me ask it this way, sir: looking at No. 204, the last name to appear on that page, we see in the first column the number 204 and then in the second column the Roman numeral (iv). Can you tell us what that Roman numeral stands for?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Can you hear us, Mr. Vujanovic? Mr. Vujanovic, can you hear us? I do not think so. Mr. Vujanovic, can you hear us? Mr. Marro, can you hear us? I think we have lost sound. They have lost sound.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I hear you. I hear you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARRO
utterances.text: No problem, your Honour. Everything is fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Vujanovic, now that we can hear one another, I would like you to look at the bottom of the page. We see the number 204 and then in the column next to it there appears to be the Roman numeral (iv) or (iv). In any event, can you tell us what that refers to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is Roman numeral (iv). The entire area of the city is divided into several districts, but this is one of the districts where duty was performed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: So I see as we look up the page that next to the number 201, in the column next to that there also appears the Roman numeral (iv)? I take that again refers to that ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is the same number.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Again refers to that particular district?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I think the witness is looking at 2nd September.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: No, he appears to have the right Exhibit. Do you have 78B before you, Mr. Vujanovic?

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Your Honour, he has the right Exhibit but the wrong column.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I understand the objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Vujanovic, let me ask you to look up the page to the police officer who is indicated by No. 201? That is the name Bozo. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I see it. I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: In the column immediately next to the number 201 there appears the Roman numeral (iv).

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Does that again refer to a particular district in the town?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it refers to the same part as (iv) under (1) does.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: That district is what? Where is that district?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is the area of the town itself, that is to say, the railway station, the bus station, in Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I note that next to some of the numbers no Roman numeral appears, for example, next to No. 200 or next to No. 199?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can say in order to facilitate work I just put this there for my own convenience. It is not a special designation. It was just for me to make things easier for me, that is, to put in the right entries in this work list.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What is written in that same column next to 203 in Dusko Tadic's row?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: "Dez" -- it is some kind of abbreviation.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What does it represent or stand for?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At present I cannot tell, because we had a lot of information involved that were of interest to us and also on the preceding page when we looked at remarks, probably I took something out of there and put certain things in there before No. 203.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Do you know for sure that the writing in that column that says "Dez" is your handwriting?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can guarantee that for sure, my handwriting, and also this entire list that I have on the table.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: In the row immediately above 203 and 202, it appears that next to that number in the column for position is the number 1 or perhaps you can read it better on your copy?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes, it is number 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What information did that provide you? How did that assist you or what shorthand was that for the information you were recording?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Otherwise that is not entered into that. You put in functions, designations, so this is nothing to do with the service itself. This is for internal use only -- simply things that I had to take out of this list for myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: In that case, in the column next to 202, what did the "1" stand for?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Also I cannot remember all the information that I got out of that list then. I do not know what are all the data I needed and why I put it in.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I understand. Again looking at row No. 203, Dusko Tadic's row and drawing ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: --- your attention to September 5th where it is indicated "nije radio", I believe you said that the information that Mr. Tadic did not work on that day came from the leader of the shift. How do you know that information came from the leader of the shift rather than from the information you received from the daily schedule which was prepared by the station Commander?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: According to the daily schedule ----

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay, the way we are proceeding now, it appears we are not going to finish Friday with video link. We had set aside an extra day, Saturday, if we had to because that is all the time that we had got from the donated time and equipment. Am I correct that it looks like we will have to sit on Saturday?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I think we are going to be all right by Friday, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: You think so? OK. Mr. Tieger and Mr. Niemann, you have asked that some of these witnesses -- not all these witnesses -- two witnesses we have heard thus far, at least, not be released. So, if you intend on recalling them, it would have to be via video link. Once again we only have until Saturday. As we have indicated, we do not have equipment and it is not something we contemplated, but we did make arrangements for the Defence. I do not know what we can do after Saturday. So if you do want to recall any of these witnesses, perhaps you should talk with the Defence and see if you can reach some agreement to either recall them out of time or something. All I am saying is we just have the equipment through Saturday and I do not know what we will do after that. You think about it and let me know something tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Vujanovic, can you hear us?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can hear you fine.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger, continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Vujanovic, would you like me to repeat the question or do you recall exactly what it was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The question relates to September 5th, where it was registered that Tadic did not work that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: That is right. The question is how do you know that that information simply was not provided to you on the daily schedule prepared by the shift Commander?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The basis of the schedule prepared by the Commander of the station, the officer on duty sends every policeman to his duty and then afterwards it is supposed to be registered that he reported in for duty, and that he was sent off to work. So his number is encircled or not and that is why it says here that he did not work that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What if the station Commander had simply not scheduled him for work that day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The Commander of the shift does not plan at all. He only implements what the station Commander plans.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I assume there were some days on which the station Commander decided that some officers would not work?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On that day when a certain policeman does not work, then a special entry is made that he is off that day, free, and then hours cannot be entered into this list.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: May I ask you to turn your attention to the last entries to the right in that row, in row 203. We see ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: --- different numbers that appear there. In the total number of hours on duty we see the No. 64. Then in the "remarks" section we see 7, 57 and 7. What does the 57 and 7 represent?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: "P" stands for "pozorna sluzba", guard duty. "7" is the 7 -- duty is the seven services, and then "57" is the number of hours, and the "7" below is seven hours before reporting for duty, he is supposed to report for duty half an hour earlier, and then whenever he works for seven hours, then he has to report an hour -- half an hour before that. So, all of these hours are added up.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: So for each shift every police officer receives additional time for the period before actually being at the duty station?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, these are the hours of preparing for duty.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: You have indicated that it was the responsibility of the shift leader to report whether or not all the members of the shift had shown up for work?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: First of all, how large were these shifts? How many officers on each shift or did that vary?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was a certain number.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Do you know, for example, how many officers in sector 4?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am not aware of this information.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What if during the course of that shift one of the officers went out, left the area for, let us say, a cup of coffee or a bite to eat, is that something that the shift leader would necessarily record?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Every policeman has to report before leaving his duty station. He has to the report to the shift Commander about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Sure, and did the shift Commander have to report to you on each occasion that a police officer went out to get a cup of coffee for himself or for his fellow officers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, he did not have to inform me, but he had to inform his superiors of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I take it the same thing would be true if one of the officers on duty was not feeling well for an hour or two; that is something he should tell his shift leader but the shift leader would not necessarily have to report to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He is duty bound to report to the shift leader and the shift leader can release him, but in that case he has to report to the Commander of the station about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Depending on the amount of time, either the shift leader or the station Commander might not bring that information to your attention, correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They would not tell me.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What if one of the officers on duty was sent to an assignment in another sector, that is something that his shift leader would have to know about under the rules but about which you would not necessarily be informed, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In order to change duty, mean duty is assigned on the basis of a list, a schedule, and then the Commander has to be made aware of all that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Assuming the particular officer notified the shift leader and assuming the shift leader notified the station Commander, the station Commander would not necessarily notify you that the officer had performed some function in another area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They would not have to inform me.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Do you know what the boundaries of sector 4 were, physical boundaries?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is the area that includes the bus station and the railway station. It is a very small area.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Was that a particular position at the bus station or railway station?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there were definite positions.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: At different times would the officers patrolling the bus station and railway station be in different positions?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, they would work together in that sector.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Would they stand at exactly the same spot for the entire portion of their shift or would they patrol the area, or do you know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They have an office there and, if necessary, they do patrol the region together.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Is it fair to say that sometimes some of the officers would be inside the office and others would be outside engaged in some form of patrol?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mostly they were obliged to perform their duties together.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: You yourself never performed any patrol duties for the Prijedor police station, did you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Nothing further, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Nothing arising, your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Is there any objection to this witness being permanently excused?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Vujanovic, you are free to leave now. However, you may be recalled as a witness, so you should make yourself available if you are asked to return to give testimony for the Tribunal. So, please keep in touch with Mr. Wladimiroff and he will contact you if you are to return to give additional testimony. Will you do that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There are no problems. Whenever necessary, I shall be available.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much for coming, Mr. Vujanovic. You are now excused.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you too. (The witness withdrew).

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay, would you call your next witness, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour. As a preliminary matter, first of all, I have had a communication from Banja Luka that Mr. Prpos has been able to have supplied the unredacted Exhibits which, I believe, are in the possession, joint possession, of Defence and Prosecution as well as including the page relating to 3rd August which, your Honours may remember, questions were asked about. DRAGOLJUB SAVIC, called.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Marro, you may administer the oath, if you wish, and then ask the witness to be seated. Never mind. Have the witness seated. Be seated. We are discussing another matter. Mr. Marro, you may administer the oath to Mr. Savic unless he has already administered the oath.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Need we discuss this before this witness? I understand those documents are available.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I will raise it later, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: OK. Very good. You may proceed. Wait, before we proceed, we have received an affidavit Mr. Kay, regarding Mr. Savic and Mr. Budimir. I presume you will then make an oral motion for Mr. Savic to give his testimony by video conference?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your Honour, that was our intent, if I may replicate now what is on that document as part of our motion, that we need to call this witness by video link.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Is there any objection from the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Your Honour, we have not been served with anything in relation to this.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Would you provide the Prosecution with a copy of the affidavit or do you have an extra one?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your Honour, we left it with the Registry.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: It has just been served.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I have not seen it, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I have not marked on this one.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I have had the list with the name on it for some time. (Handed).

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: We will be a few moments, Mr. Savic. You may just sit there. Thank you. Mr. Niemann?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Yes, your Honours. Your Honours, we have heard something in relation to police officers being not permitted to testify, but this is the first time there has ever been reference, so far as we know, to civil servants. From our understanding of the evidence, at least one other witness, as we understand the position of that other witness, would have been a civil servant.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: You do not mean I would have to give the name?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: No, it was Witness D, your Honour, and it was in closed session or private session, at least. So we are somewhat perplexed to now learn that this is a new development that we have not been informed of before.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: So what is the position regarding Mr. Savic?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Witness D worked for the municipality, if your Honour will recollect. This witness works for the railway board of Prijedor and Banja Luka, and was spoken to during the summer. The information passed on to me yesterday and to Miss de Bertodano was that permissions would be not forthcoming from the Ministry for this witness to be able to leave Republika Srpska to give evidence; hence the filing of the affidavit this morning. It is also believed that the same position will apply to that witness Budimir whom I have not heard that we have been in contact yet with, and enquiries are taking place on the ground in Banja Luka by Mr. Wladimiroff during this week. He works for the Ministry of Defence.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: When was Mr. Savic -- I am looking for his name on the witness list and I cannot see it -- is it on this green sheet which was the list that you filed?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I do not have that to hand.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I do not see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I doubt it because ----

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: He is not listed on the list that was filed sometime ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No, he arises as a result of continuing Defence investigations that have been up until even as we speak.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I am sure, as long as we continue both sides will be investigating and continuing, but at some point we have to say "no", it comes to an end. We are about at that point. He is not on the list that you filed September 27th.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: But he is someone you have discovered and you have also discovered that his boss or the person in charge has said he will not be allowed to come.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: So, therefore, we need to hear his testimony via video link. What is the importance of his testimony?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: He gives details of train times for 23rd May 1992 and 15th June 1992 which are relevant to the defendant's alibi.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: May 23rd?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, the day before the conflict in Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Did they not arrive with the priest?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No, your Honour, that was earlier in May, May 8th. Your Honour, the story, so to speak, is still unfolding and more Defence witnesses are to be heard on this matter.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Please do not tell me that. Mr. Niemann, train times, May -- what did you say -- 23rd and June 15th?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: 15th June.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: June 15th.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Your Honours, our concern at the moment was just with this change of circumstances. We were informed that this witness would be called at 10 a.m. on 15th which was yesterday. How long the Defence have known of the witness, I do not know. I am unsure now, having regard to what Mr. Kay has stated, what the position is with the witness Budimir.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I wanted to ask about Budimir. Budimir was listed and listed as a policy witness, is that not so? Where did I get that information from?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I have scribbled on my sheet "policy". Is that not someone -- you know, we heard from the Prosecution policy for several days ----

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You have heard 16 policy witnesses.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: --- and we have heard your witnesses, a witness at least, policy. Is this not someone who could come here -- the reason I ask is video conferencing is very expensive and it is also not even called for, so we are making an exception but we do not want to wear out the use of this unless it is absolutely necessary. So it is not really for convenience because no one, I am sure, would want to come to the Hague if they could choose -- I might not either!

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: He is someone within the government, so to speak, and whose authority comes from the Ministry of Defence.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Budimir, you are telling me, cannot come?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: That is my information. Enquiries are being made, as your Honours know. We cannot just telephone these people up to speak to them. It is ----

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: No, we have seen that both sides have the same problem. I understand the problem, but understand our limitations. Mr. Savic, though, is listed -- I asked this morning -- you said half an hour to an hour he will talk about train times. I will overrule your objection and we will hear from Mr. Savic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I am much obliged.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Budimir, I would ask you, you have listed him for three hours, at least when I asked you about him, so really investigate and see if, perhaps, we can handle it in a different way. We will decide on Mr. Budimir when we get there. Mr. Marro, would you please put the earphones on Mr. Savic?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay, you may begin.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Mr. Savic, can you give the Court your full name, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Savic Dragoljub.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can you tell the Court what is your job?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am an economist.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can you tell the Court whom you work for?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I work in the Doboj transport company, the section for Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Is that the railway company?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is the railway company.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Have you looked at the train timetable for 23rd May 1992 ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: --- for the train from Banja Luka to Prijedor and Prijedor to Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The train going from Prijedor to Banja Luka and Banja Luka to Prijedor is given in the information submitted to you. The departure times from Banja Luka and arrival time in Prijedor and vice versa. Those are the data that I have given you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, and if you would just answer my questions about it, I would be much obliged. First of all, can you tell us what document you looked at to provide a schedule of the train times on 23rd May 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The document from which I gathered the information is the daily record on the movement of trains in the station of Prijedor. That is the document I used.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can you confirm that the trains were running between those two towns on that date of 23rd May?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: According to the records that I had at my disposal and from which I collected the information, yes, one can see that they were running.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did you do a similar schedule for trains between Banja Luka and Prijedor for 15th June 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, the timetable was the same then as it is now, that there is no war.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can you confirm that the trains were running between Banja Luka and Prijedor on that date of 15th June?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do confirm on the basis of the records. At that time I was not performing the duty I have been performing since 1st August 1996. Therefore, I submitted the information on the basis of the records kept.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did the records that were kept also indicate the number of the train that was running at a particular time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The records show the number of the train, the departure time or arrival time, depending on the direction in which the train was running. We can see from the records the time of departure and of arrival.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did the information that you looked at also give information concerning delay from the original timetable?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is recorded if there are any delays, plus 45 minutes, for instance, or something like that. "Plus 45", that means a delay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The information you looked at to compile your schedule, was that made by someone who had the responsibility to record these matters?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, the information is entered by the assistant chief of the station.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: What I would like you to do now is to look at documents in a folder called E1. If Mr. Marro could put those documents in front of you? Do you recognise the document which is of two pages placed in front of you as the schedule that you have compiled with the information you have told us about?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is the schedule.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I now offer this to the Court as D79A in a form of Serbo-Croat and D79B as an English translation.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: What is this that you are offering now?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: It is a schedule of train times for 23rd May 1992 and 15th June 1992 compiled as described by Mr. Savic. 79A is the Serbo-Croat, 79B is the English translation.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger, is there any objection to 79A and B?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: They will be admitted. These are printed, published timetables?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: OK. That is probably -- maybe we could take judicial notice of something like this. In any case, proceed along.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I do not think Mr. Kay intended to indicate that.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Yes. I thought they were -- he said "yes" only because I am looking at the second page. But then this witness said that he was not even in a position to record these. I am really trying to hurry the testimony along. I will let it unfold.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Savic, can you look at the document which is headed 23rd May 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am looking at it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Does that contain a schedule of the times of departures and arrivals of trains at Prijedor railway station on that date ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: --- to Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is a list of a train arrivals and departures on the Prijedor railway station on 23rd May 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Those are the trains to Banja Luka and from Banja Luka on that date?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Also if we just look at the timings of the trains, the first one was scheduled to depart for Banja Luka at 5.45 in the morning, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there was a delay of 45 minutes. It should have left at 5.00, so it actually left at 5.45.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Seeing that information concerning the delay on that date of 23rd May, does that indicate that someone has taken notice of the fact that the train actually ran on that date?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is recorded as having been delayed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Does it show that the next train that departed for Banja Luka from Prijedor on 23rd May is recorded as having departed at 12.25 in the afternoon?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it left on 12.25.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I would like you now to look at the schedule for 15th June 1992. Does that contain the same information between those towns of Prijedor and Banja Luka for the running of the trains on that day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Here we have information on arrival and departure of trains for that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: This record containing these times of arrival and departure, do they show the arrival at Prijedor railway station before the departure to Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: For instance, if we look at ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It shows that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: For instance, if we look at the train No. 940 ----

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: --- it states arrival 6.48?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, arrival 6.45, departure 7.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Is that arrival at Prijedor railway station?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, arrival at the station, then stays there for a while and then it leaves.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: So the departure column shows the time that it departs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Is this an accurate schedule that you have prepared for both of these dates?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The record was taken from the log book recording the arrival and departure of trains in the Prijedor station, prepared by the assistant station chief. This is a copy of those records.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. That is all I ask.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: Can I ask you just to clarify one thing? Does it mean, when it is departure, does it go back to Banja Luka or does it continue on? I see sometimes there is only two minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Savic, can you clarify a further matter for us?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The arrivals column which contains a time, for instance, the 940 train on 23rd May 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: When it arrives at Prijedor railway station at 6.42, can you see that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. When it departs at 6.43 ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not understand. It arrives at 6.42 and it left at 6.43.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Perhaps you can tell us, first of all, where it arrives from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It arrives from Banja Luka, and from Prijedor it goes on to Novi Grad or Bosanski Novi.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: So at 6.43 that train would have left Prijedor to go to Bosanski Novi or elsewhere?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it goes on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. Wait there, please.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour. Mr. Savic, is it correct that the schedules for the train that we see on the documents you presented have remained, essentially, in effect to this day? Did I understand that you indicated that these are basically the same schedules that have remained in effect since the time indicated on the documents you prepared?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Roughly the timetable is as it is according to this document. Of course, changes are always possible, as in any other job. There are changes in arrivals and departures, these are possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Do you know for how long before May 23rd this was the basic schedule for a train service between Prijedor and Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: So, this would have been, essentially, the same schedule that the trains between Prijedor and Banja Luka followed on 23rd May, 24th, 25th, 26th May and on to this day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, up to this day, more or less.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
