utterances.text: I understand that you reviewed a document which was prepared by somebody else and from that information prepared the document which you have presented to the Defence, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, on the basis of that document I prepared this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Is there any reason why you did not simply copy the document that you were looking at and present that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There is no reason, except that that is a book. So I had no other way but to copy it from the book. I just confirm the information found in the book.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Looking at the schedule which you prepared for June 15th, that indicates, as I read it, that each and every train arrived on time and departed on time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is what the record says.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Do you know whether or not the trains performed with that kind of precision and punctuality or whether or not the person at the train station simply did not record any deviations from the schedule?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: How long does a train take to go from Prijedor to Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The train takes from Prijedor to Banja Luka about one hour, one and a half. It depends on the circumstances. Everything is changing, the condition of the railroad and the situation and then the speed has to be reduced and so on. So an hour and a half.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Is the time from Banja Luka to Prijedor the same or are there any factors which make the time it takes to go in that direction different?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The time depends on the segment of the railroad, because in some segments the speed is lower and then it takes longer. Then there are other parts of the railroad that are in better condition, and then the trip takes less. Therefore, it all depends on the technical conditions on the railroad on which the traffic is running.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I am asking you about the segment between Prijedor and Banja Luka and between Banja Luka and Prijedor. Are you indicating that there are factors on any given day which may change the amount of time it takes, that those factors may change in any given day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The factors that affect that are the railroad itself possibly, and sometimes there is no electricity and whatever. Sometimes something goes wrong with the train itself. These are some of the characteristics that can affect the time needed for the train to traverse that part of the railway, not only that part of the railroad.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: In general, however, the time between Prijedor and Banja Luka is an hour to an hour and a half, as you indicated?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Is the time from Banja Luka to Prijedor, essentially, the same?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is more or less the same time. I cannot tell you in terms of exact minutes, but it is more or less the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Excuse me, may I have a quick moment to look at the schedule? Thank you, your Honour. That is all I have.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Nothing arises, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Savic, does the train go from Prijedor to Omarska?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From Prijedor to Omarska?

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Now the train goes from Prijedor to Omarska, now at this time.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: How long is the train trip from Prijedor to Omarska?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From Prijedor to Omarska it takes about 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: How often ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 20 to 25 minutes.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Is it the same amount of time going from Omarska to Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: How often does the train run from Prijedor to Omarska?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: All these trains go through Omarska and to Omarska. The train from Banja Luka to Prijedor goes through Omarska.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: So this, if I look at this list that you prepared from the train schedule, then I could assume that the train from -- well, I guess the train for Banja Luka No. 6421, is that one that would originate in, well, at some point it would be in Prijedor and then stop in Omarska on its way to Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, in Omarska, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Then from Banja Luka it would stop in Omarska and then eventually it would get to Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: OK, thank you. All of these trains, do they all stop at Omarska?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They do.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay, do you have additional questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Nothing arises, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger? OK. Is there any objection to Mr. Savic being permanently excused?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Savic, you are permanently excused. That means you are free to leave. Thank you very much for coming.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay, would you call your next witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The next witness is Trivo Reljic.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Marro, would you administer the oath, please, to Mr. Reljic? TRIVO RELJIC, called.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay, you may begin.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Is your name Trivo Reljic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My name is Trivo Reljic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Do you live in Svodna?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I live in Svodna.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: How old are you, Mr. Reljic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am about to turn 62.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: What is your job?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A medical technician.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Are you employed or unemployed at the moment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have just retired now.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: For how long have you lived in Svodna?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was born in Svodna and I lived there until 1958. From '58 to '72 (sic) I lived in Kozarac and now I live in Svodna again.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did you live in Kozarac until '72 or 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: '92, until 23rd May 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Until that date, had you lived in the village of Kozarac with your family?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did your family consist of a wife and two sons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, my wife Milka, my son Goran, my son Zoran.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Is it right that one of your sons is severely disabled?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Zoran, my son Zoran. He uses a wheelchair.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did you work as a medical technician in the clinic in Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, all the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: When did you start that job at the clinic in Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 1st April 1958.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: When did you finish that job in Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On 23rd May 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Why did you cease living in Kozarac on that day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On 23rd everything was abandoned in Kozarac. This war was breaking out and that is how I went to Svodna where I was born. I went with my family.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Are you a Serb?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did your wife leave Kozarac on 23rd May with you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: On 23rd May can you tell us what time you left Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Around 20 minutes to 7 in the morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Where did you go to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I started going towards Prijedor and from Prijedor I went to Svodna.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: How did you travel there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We had a car, a so-called Fica, Fiat 850. My son was driving it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Who was in the car with you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My son and I, we left in the morning and we drove Dusko Tadic to Prijedor with his family.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: When you ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: With his family.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: When you drove Dusko Tadic, did you leave from your house with him or did you meet him somewhere?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was going out of my yard, and since the house of Dusko Tadic is across the street from the place where I lived, then Dusko showed up and he said, "Where are you going?" and I said, "To Prijedor". "Could I come with you?" "Well, you could", and we took him to Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: What time did you arrive at Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter cannot hear the witness. There is no sound. There has just been a bit of sound, says the English interpreter.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Mr. Reljic, we lost your evidence to us then and I am going to have to repeat the question and if you could give us your answer again? What time did you arrive in Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From Kozarac to Prijedor we travelled about 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did Dusko Tadic travel to Svodna with you or did he go anywhere else?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We left him near the Autotransport company in Prijedor. He stayed there and we continued our journey.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Whereabouts in Prijedor is the Autotransport company?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Up by the hospital, the so-called Urije.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did you leave Dusko Tadic on his own or did anyone else also get left with him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: For the time being he was alone when we left.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: So who else was left in your car?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I, my son, my wife and the other son, the sick one.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: So Dusko Tadic then travelled with you on his own with your family?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Were other Serbs leaving Kozarac at this time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as I know, some of them left the same morning and the others stayed on. Whether they stayed throughout the day and throughout the night, I do not know because I left.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Had other Muslims who lived in Kozarac left the town before this time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Some of them left and some stayed at home and others were moving towards the forest up there towards Kozara. They were moving away. They were thinking that a fight would break out. There it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. That is all I ask. Wait there, please, Mr. Reljic.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger, cross-examination of Mr. Reljic or Miss Hollis?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Mr. Reljic, could you give us your exact date of birth, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 16th April 1935 in Svodna.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: You indicated that when you lived in Kozarac you lived across from the home of Dule Tadic, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What was your address in Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Marsala Tita, No. 3, and after that just before the war broke out they renamed it into Mladena Stojanovica, also No. 3.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: So you lived across from the Tadic family home?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you know the members of the Tadic family?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, yes, we knew each other as neighbours. It was nearby, just across the street, so we knew each other.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Who did you know in the Tadic family?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I knew the father, Ostoja, and Staka, the mother, brother Stojan, Mladen.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you know Dule Tadic's wife Mira?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, we worked together in the clinic for some time.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Your wife Milka, where was she born?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: She was born ----

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The English interpreter did not get any more sound.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: I am sorry, sir. We could not hear the last part of your answer. Could you tell us again where was your wife born?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The village of Brdjani in Kozarac, in the forest, in the mountains.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Again there is no sound.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What was her maiden name? I am sorry, sir. We did not hear your answer. Could you repeat that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Petric Mile, Milka. Petric was her surname and Mile was her father's name.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What were the dates of birth for your sons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Zoran was born on May 26th, '61. Goran was born on 30th November in 1968.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did either of your sons serve in the military in 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My older son did not and my younger son, Goran, also was not in the army then. He went to the army in 1994.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you know a man by the name of Sreto Karajica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Karajica, yes, he worked with me. I know him.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Where was he from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From Trnopolje, the village of Trnopolje, Kozarac also.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: In 1992 what would his age have been, if you know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot tell exactly how old he was.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Was he approximately your age or younger?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Younger. He was born in '46. I know that.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What was his father's name, if you know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sveto.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: That would be S ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sveto Karajica.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: That would be S-V-E-T-O, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did Sveto have any brothers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He had a brother. I do not know what his name is. I forgot. He is disabled. There is something wrong with his foot or leg.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did Sreto have any sons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, two sons.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Do you recall their names?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mladen and -- Mladen and Zoran.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Do you know what their ages would have been in 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In '68, one of them, and the younger one, I cannot tell exactly. I do not know when he was born.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Sir, can you tell us the month and the year that you retired?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This year I applied for retirement on 1st January of 1996.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: You had been working in what town prior to your retirement, in Svodna?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I did not work when I came. I was waiting because there was not any work.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: But up until recently, up until you retired, where were you working?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I worked in Kozarac. I worked only for six months in Bosanski Novi before coming to Kozarac. That is what I did only.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Sir, what I am interested in is you indicated that you worked in Kozarac and then in May 1992 you left Kozarac. Have you worked since May 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I only came to Prijedor to work in the health centre for 12 days. They -- I had no vehicle to travel by, so they let me be on the waiting list, so to speak.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: During the months of May to December 1992, how easy was it for you to get fuel for your personal vehicle?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know. I did not buy it and I could not afford it, and my son would not drive either, so ----

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Was fuel rationed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: --- there was no fuel.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When you would travel from Svodna, did you have to get special permission to travel from Svodna to another town?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not ask for that. I only got this paper in order to go to work. When I went to work for 12 days, I just got this paper that I would be going to work.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When you left Kozarac on 23rd May, did you get a paper giving you permission to leave the town?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I did not get any document then.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: I believe you indicated it took you approximately 20 minutes to go from Kozarac to Prijedor, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Something like that, because we stopped for a moment because my son recognised a colleague of his. Then we stopped. He exchanged a couple of words with him and then we went on.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Where was it that you stopped?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Near the hospital in Prijedor, it is called Cirkin Polje, the locality, that is where we stopped, on the road.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Who was it that your son recognised?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A colleague of his. They went to school together in the forestry school when they were students and they recognised each other.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: That was the only stop that you made between Kozarac and Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, only one stop.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Just for a point of clarification: early in your testimony you indicated that when you left Kozarac on 23rd May you took with you Dule Tadic and his family, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, not his family, just Dusko Tadic and my family.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: No further questions, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Could the car that you were travelling in have accommodated both of your families?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, it could not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: On your way to Prijedor from Kozarac on 23rd May, did you have to pass through any checkpoints?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. We passed through at Koncari. There were Muslims unloading two trucks, weapons and I do not know what, and at Orlovci there was a checkpoint of the police and we passed by that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did you have to stop at Orlovci checkpoint?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Nothing. We just waved our hands out of the car and passed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. That is all I ask.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Miss Hollis, do you have additional questions?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Sir, so when you were by the Orlovci checkpoint you did not have to stop and show your papers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, we did not.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: You just merely waved and went through the checkpoint, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, we just said "hello" because we had no papers.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Nothing arises, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Is there any objection to Mr. Reljic being permanently excused?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Reljic, you are free to leave now. However, you may be recalled to give testimony for the Tribunal. So you should make yourself available. Keep in touch with Mr. Wladimiroff and he will tell you if you are asked to return to give testimony. Will you do that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If necessary, I am here.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much for coming, Mr. Reljic. You are excused now, but not permanently.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay, would you call your next witness, please?

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Your Honour, the next witness is Stojan Smoljic. STOJAN SMOLJIC, called.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Marro, you may administer the oath to Mr. Smoljic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Miss de Bertodano, you may begin if we have sound. It is clear to me.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Witness, is your name Stojan Smoljic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Where do you live?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: What is your present occupation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I beg your pardon?

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: What is your job?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am not doing anything now. I used to work for the Electricity Board of Jajce. That is where I was born and I came here in '92.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: When did you come here, on what date in 1992 did you come to Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On 15th October I came alone to see whether there was any accommodation to be found for my family. After that Dusan Tadic was the Secretary of the local community and he took me in. Then I went back ----

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Mr. Smoljic ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: --- to bring my family.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: --- if I could stop you. If I could take you back a couple of stages. Why did you come from Jajce to Kozarac on 15th October?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Because I was chased out by the Muslims and Croats and they killed my cousin.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: You said you came on your own to Kozarac on 15th October, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On 15th October I came alone and on 28th October I brought my family, because there was nowhere for them to live.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: How long did you stay having arrived on 15th October before you returned to collect your family?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I stayed one and a half days or rather 24 hours.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Did you find accommodation during that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Dusan Tadic found accommodation for me, and then I returned to paint the house with my family and that is where I am now in Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: How did you meet Dusko Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I met him because he was the Secretary of the local community.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Did you meet him then on the day that you arrived on 15th October?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Where did you meet him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I met him at the school where the local community was housed.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: You have told us that he found you accommodation, and you then returned to Jajce to collect your family?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: You returned to the Kozarac area on 28th October, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Did you after returning ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I returned on 17th October and then I came again with my whole family on 28th October.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: How many people are there in your family who came with you on 28th October?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There is me, my wife and six children.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: When you returned on 28th October, did you find any employment in Kozarac after that date?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, there was nothing to be done, nothing was functioning. I could not find any work. I do not know what will happen to me because I was a worker of Elektro Bosna of Jajce.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Have you done any work at all since 28th October?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Here I help people and they help me, so that me and my family can survive somehow.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: In the time that you were in Kozarac after 28th October, did you see Dusko Tadic again?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I saw him every day and he would ask me every day, "Stojan, do your children have anything to eat and do you have any problems?" And through the humanitarian aid he received he supplied all the refugees. He did not care what ethnic group they belonged to. They offered Croats just as much as he offered me, precisely because they were of another ethnic group so that no one could reproach him. Therefore, I got to know him as a humane individual.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Where would you see him in Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the school or he travelled by bus. He did not have a car of his own. So he would use the bus regularly. His flat was in Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Do you know how often he came to Kozarac from Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Regularly, and he would leave regularly too.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: How many times a week, approximately, would he come to Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He would come in the morning and then he would go about midday, 2 or 3 o'clock when the bus left, I do not know exactly. Then he would come back in the morning and so on.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Do you know whether he ever stayed in Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot remember, nor did I notice him staying.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Do you remember when he left Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know, only when I saw this case with him on television, this surprised me. I did not know of this.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: When did you ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know what happened and what is happening now and all this. It was a great surprise to me what happened to him.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Can you remember for how long it was that you used to see Dusko Tadic on a regular basis?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Whenever I needed help I would go to him, and I would find him personally in his office.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Can you remember over what period of time you used to see him in Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think it was the autumn, until the autumn, even it was winter time too.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: You have told us that you arrived in October. Did you continue to see Dusko Tadic during the rest of that year?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Did you see him during the following year 1993?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Can you recall when he left Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That I do not know, only when he said, "I will not be staying here for long, I have to go to Prijedor", he just told me that he does not like the war, absolutely not, nor the front.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Nothing further, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Smoljic, where was the accommodation that you eventually found in Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In Hasana Husinica Street.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I am going to try to place that without the need to refer to a map, if we can. Can you describe for us where your house is relative to Marsala Tita Street, to the main street of Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Just below the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: So, is it on the street which runs between the hospital and the church, or is it on a street going in the other direction?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The other street, the blind alley. There is no asphalt. It is a short street. You go under the hospital and in this way it is a short street.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were you told who owned that house before you did, before you occupied it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I was not told but I learned later.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: How did you learn?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I learned that, men told me who had worked with those people ----

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Who had ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: --- that they were good people.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Who was the owner of that house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Beslagic Hakija and Beslagic Hilmija.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you learn their nationalities?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Now you spoke about Dusko Tadic's position with the Local Commune. Who were the other officials of the Kozarac area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was a Danijela, I forget her surname, a Montenegrin called Cedo, Borko Dragicevic. They were there.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: The transcript or at least we heard you as saying "Borko" Dragicevic. Is it possible that first name is Bosko?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: During the times you would see Dusko Tadic in October and November, what was he wearing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was wearing civilian clothes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: You indicated that you would see him whenever you needed help. During the time after you arrived in Kozarac you were looking for a job, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, nothing was functioning then and I am still waiting. I should have gone before a disability commission to give me an easier job because I am disabled or to give me a disability pension, but I do not know what is going to happen to me. Where have I been? - nowhere. What have I been doing? - nothing.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you travel out of Kozarac to look for work?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, not yet because I co-operate with my neighbours and somehow we get along. I get some humanitarian relief and we are somehow surviving.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Can you describe the premises of the Local Commune in October 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On the first floor, up the stairs and then to the right.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What other offices or persons were located in the same building in October 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In which building, the school? There was a police checkpoint and then they moved further down towards the veterinarian station.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Now the humanitarian -- I am sorry, let me ask you one more question. Were there any other officers or officials located in the school?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: The humanitarian aid that was distributed to you, where did that come from, if you know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From the humaneness of the world.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Do you know whether or not that came from Prijedor, Banja Luka or any other part, any other area adjacent to opstina Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as I know, most of it came from Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Smoljic, on the occasions you saw Dusko Tadic ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: --- I take it that you would not see him at the moment he arrived in Kozarac on any particular day, or on every single day he came to Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I saw him several times. Every day I would come by to see what is new, because we cleaned the school a little bit and he would call me in to help him to clean up and then he would say, "I am late for the bus", and indeed I saw him going away by bus and coming by bus in the morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: So you would be present when he arrived every morning by bus and present when he departed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would come to clean up, to help cleaning up.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: You would be there every morning when he arrived and every late morning or early afternoon when he departed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, to help him clean up. Yes, when he came in the morning I would come by to see whether he has arrived. He would come by bus. Sometimes he would come before me by bus and I would hear the bus and sometimes I was there before him.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger, would you ask him for what period of time this is. I know October/November, but was it any later? I thought the witness had testified he saw him until 1993. So I want to know how long he saw him from October through 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Smoljic, this was true for not only October and November but for what period of time? How long did you continue to see Dusko Tadic for every morning and every afternoon?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Even when the snow fell then we would be clearing up the snow around the church. So it was during the winter time too.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: When did you stop seeing Dusko Tadic every morning when he arrived and every afternoon when he left?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Because then I had work to do around my house, I did not have time to go there. Sometimes he would give me the key to clean up and I am in a hurry to catch my bus. I do not know any more. As far as I was able to see, he used the bus regularly. I do not know anything else. He would come to work and then home to where he was living in Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: When was it, what month, when you stopped seeing Dusko Tadic this regularly?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I joined up with other people to help them to cut the firewood and so on. Then I would collect firewood for myself. So I did not have time, but I cannot remember when this happened and when I heard about him. I cannot remember, but it was a shock because he made no difference between Muslims and Croats. He would give them humanitarian aid just as he gave to Serbs. In fact, he gave them more so that nobody could reproach him tomorrow. There was the Croat Grnic, you can ask them if I am not telling the truth. Whenever he was distributing aid he would give it to people who were in need.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I thought we might finish but perhaps it is better if we adjourn.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: We will adjourn until tomorrow at 10 o'clock. Mr. Smoljic, you should return back to the location where you are tomorrow, so that we can begin at 10 a.m. tomorrow. So we will adjourn until tomorrow ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: --- at 10 a.m. Mr. Niemann, tell me tomorrow what is the Prosecution's position regarding the video conferencing equipment. Thank you, sir, you are excused until tomorrow at 10 a.m.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you. The same to you. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: We will adjourn until tomorrow at 10.00 a.m.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: (The court adjourned until the following day).
